newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks hit year high in the morning.
newsitem.headline: French stocks hit year high in the morning.

text.p: French shares started with a big one percent increase on Friday and established a fresh year high for the CAC-40 at 2,239.80 before retreating slightly.

Dealers said the market was supported by Wall Street's seventh consecutive closing gain, taking the Dow Jones index over the 6,300 level for the first time, as well as by a new contract high in French bond futures.
Trading was likely to pause slightly this afternoon to evaluate a new set of U.S. statistics.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 20.81 points or 0.94 percent at 2,238.99 at 0922 GMT while the CAC-40 futures contract was up 18.5 at 2,244.5.
The French rise takes shares back to early 1994 levels. The life high, at 2,360.98, was reached on February 2, 1994.

"There was a good jump at the start, boosted by Wall Street, the T-bond and MATIF," a share dealer said, adding he expected prices to remain close to their current levels for the most of the day awaiting the new U.S. data.

Data due today are U.S. October capacity utilisation (expected at 83 pct) and industrial production (seen up 0.2 percent) as well as September business inventories (expected 0.2 percent up). In France, the August seasonally adjusted current account surplus rose to 10.40 billion francs.

"Things are calming down after the frenzy of yesterday," said a dealer. On Thursday, requoting in insurers UAP and AXA following their agreed merger through a share swap, boosted volume to a huge 9.9 billion francs, the heaviest since May 23, and among the highest this year.

LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton dropped to a low of 1,231 before regaining most of the loss to 1,250 at 0957 GMT on a newspaper report that U.S. investment bank Kohlberg Kravis Roberts & Co might bid for DFS, the U.S. duty free-chain in which LVMH is buying a 59 pct stake for 12.6 billion francs.
